extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: RoboBench is a comprehensive benchmark that systematically evaluates multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It defines five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs. The benchmark draws from large-scale real robotic data and in-house collection, covering diverse embodiments, attribute-rich objects, multi-view scenes, and memory-driven navigation. It introduces an MLLM-as-world-simulator evaluation framework for planning that assesses embodied feasibility by simulating whether predicted plans can achieve critical object-state changes under physical and visual constraints.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang; State Key Laboratory of Multimedia Information Processing, School of Computer Science, Peking University; Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence; Institute for Brain and Intelligence, Fudan University; University of Science and Technology Beijing; Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics
extraction.citeAs: Luo et al. RoboBench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brain. arXiv:2510.17801v1 [cs.RO], 20 Oct 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Datasets are built from open-source and in-house robotic data, enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations. Instruction comprehension data uses explicit instructions from daily-life scenarios and implicit rewrites via LLMs. Perception reasoning data is constructed across robotic-centric (real robot data with type and view metadata), object-centric (curated static attributes and GPT-generated functional properties), scene-centric (Gemini-segmented video steps with manual annotations), and task-centric (human-labeled bounding boxes) aspects. Generalized planning data is built from high-quality robotic videos with Gemini-generated structured annotations refined by human annotators. Affordance prediction data is sampled from the planning pool and annotated with static, dynamic, and mobile affordances. Failure analysis data includes execution-level failures from RoboMIND labeled by experts and synthesized planning-level failures.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Planning-level failure data lacks real-world examples, so planning failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order) due to lack of real-world planning failure data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Large-scale real-world robotic datasets including RH20T (Fang et al., 2023), Open X-Embodiment (Collaboration et al., 2023), RDT-1B (Liu et al., 2024b), Embodied AI datasets (Liu et al., 2024c), RoboMIND (Wu et al., 2024), AgiBot World (Bu et al., 2025), and additional datasets (Lin et al., 2024a; Mu et al., 2023; Yang et al., 2024), supplemented by in-house collection. Object attribute data from Gao et al. (2024) and GPT-generated functional properties.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Explicit task instructions are rewritten into implicit demand-based requests using LLMs. Natural language step descriptions from videos are mapped to predefined function sequences. Function arguments are instantiated with objects extracted from step descriptions. Planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order). Affordance annotations include static (contact points), dynamic (motion trajectories), and mobile (base positions) types sampled from the planning pool.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A two-stage quality control process is applied: (1) data filtering during construction using general criteria (image quality, task validity) and task-specific filters (e.g., excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks); (2) post-construction validation by 20 professionally trained annotators checking linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy is used: items all models solve correctly are removed, and items all models fail are manually reviewed and corrected. All data are standardized into multiple-choice QA or structured planning/affordance formats.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Gemini generates structured annotations from robotic videos including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata (objects, actions, scenes, embodiments), which are refined by human annotators. Each step is mapped into function templates. Human annotators label bounding boxes for task-centric perception, annotate relative positions and keypoint changes for spatial and causal reasoning, label execution-level failures from RoboMIND, and construct directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) capturing inter-step dependencies for planning evaluation. For affordance, representative frames are annotated with contact points, motion trajectories, and base positions. For quality control, 20 professionally trained annotators conduct comprehensive quality inspections.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A majority-vote strategy is used for quality control: items that all models solve correctly are removed (too easy), whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction. Human evaluation of planning data involved expert annotators assigning holistic scores (0–20) referencing ground-truth planning lists and considering skill selection, object identification, and plan executability. Pearson correlation between automated metrics and human scores is reported (r=0.83 for MLLM-as-world-simulator vs r=0.73 for LLM-based baseline).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: RoboBench provides a comprehensive scaffold to quantify high-level cognition, clarify the role of the embodied brain, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence. It aims to advance embodied AI for manipulation in dynamic, unstructured environments, which has broad implications for robotics applications in real-world settings.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Planning data primarily focuses on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing between left-right arm assignments or positional movements, which may bias cross-embodiment planning evaluation. The benchmark relies heavily on real robotic datasets which may not cover all possible scenarios, objects, or environments.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Planning-level failure data is synthesized rather than collected from real-world failures due to lack of real-world planning failure data. The benchmark covers specific embodiment types (single-arm, dual-arm, mobile manipulator, humanoid) and may not generalize to all robotic platforms. Execution-level failure diagnosis is intrinsically difficult, with even human evaluators achieving only 47.30 on this dimension.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. The benchmark is designed for evaluating instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis capabilities. It provides a leaderboard and actionable insights for advancing embodied brain development in robotic AI.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 professionally trained annotators conducted quality inspections. Expert annotators (with prior training) assigned holistic scores for human evaluation of planning data.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini (Comanici et al., 2025) for structured annotation generation from robotic videos (task summaries, step-wise instructions, metadata); GPT for generating functional object properties and distractors; VLMs and detection models for annotation assistance.
